Dr Makhosi Khoza speaks truth to power

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Dr Makhosi Khoza puts her life on the line to speak truth to power

Further information:
The ANC powers that be have yet to make a decision on whether to discipline ANC MP Makhosi Khoza for her outspokenness outside official governing party structures – from calling for a secret ballot in the vote of no confidence in President Jacob Zuma on 8 August, to some sharply critical comments on the troubled state of the ANC and its MPs.
Described by ANC Chief Whip Jackson Mthembu as “extremely ill-disciplined” for her public comments on the sidelines of last week’s ANC national policy conference, the ANC in Parliament on Tuesday confirmed the matter has been referred up to Luthuli House head office for a decision on what to do next. Not only has Mthembu taken exception, it is understood also that ANC Secretary-General Gwede Mantashe is annoyed.
After Mthembu issued a scathing media statement, saying his MP was casting aspersions on the morality of party colleagues – “We have again spoken to comrade Khoza and raised our extreme discomfort with her utterances in relation to caucus and the leadership of the ANC at large” – Khoza took to Facebook, again:
“Is it really ill-discipline or liberation struggle credentials’ fatigue that keeps us imagining unity when we are clearly no longer pursuing the same mission? Is it ill-discipline or daring to tackle the big elephant in the room… Is it extreme ill-discipline to be intolerant of bad leadership and to uphold the Constitution? Is it ill-discipline to elect principles and ditching destructive personalities?”
It’s not necessarily a case of going rogue. For Khoza, speaking out is also a way to protect herself. She’s received death threats while on a parliamentary oversight trip to Limpopo, has threats directed at her daughter and has faced other bullying tactics, like the provincial ANC Youth League posting her home address on social media.
“I remain vulnerable and living under constant attacks, life threats and insults. No protection has been provided to me by Parliament though the ANC knows the volatility of my province, KZN (KwaZulu-Natal). The only reason I’m probably still alive is the heightened alertness of the public on my safety. Let me thank you South Africans for your overwhelming support,” Khoza wrote on Facebook last week. “It should be recalled that I opened two criminal cases at the police stations in Hillcrest and Limpopho [sic] after receiving death threats which have not stopped. I’m continuously stalked and intimidated for voicing my views on the vote of no confidence matter on a daily basis.”
On Tuesday she was accompanied by one of those, whom she described as “some volunteers” looking after her. One of the “volunteers” looked somewhat perturbed at Khoza being mobbed, including by a group of youngsters wanting a selfie, or two or three, and her handling of a tricky question. “Why should my parents vote?” Co-incidentally, her response was, of course they must vote.
The conundrum on a vote of conscience or toeing the party line Khoza faces is not hers alone. Also in a tight spot are several other ANC MPs who have expressed their disquiet privately and publicly.
Ditto members of the ANC alliance partners, the South African Communist Party (SACP) and trade union federation Cosatu, who have come to Parliament on an ANC ticket. Will the ANC line prevail, or will it be the resolutions of their organisations which both called for Zuma to step down that prevail? In the SACP at least there are ongoing discussions around this, according to at least one insider, although only Sunday’s closing of the SACP congress will show whether the self-proclaimed workers’ vanguard will take a firm resolution on how to cast the no-confidence ballot.
Speaking out, like cleaning up the web of patronage-related tenders, can be a dangerous business in a party in which factionalism often goes hand in hand with violence. The SACP has objected to protests outside the house of its Second Deputy General-Secretary Solly Mapaila, the face of anti-state capture from within the alliance, but also violence against its members in Mpumalanga and last year’s killings in KwaZulu-Natal’s Inchanga. Police a year ago announced they were investigating 29 politically motivated killings and attempted murders, including of municipal managers and councillors. In late May this year, Police Minister Fikile Mbalula announced a task-team to look particularly at such killings in KwaZulu-Natal.
Sometimes the response is more verbal as criticism itself becomes a tool in the current factional battles. Zuma delivered a snotklap to ANC veterans, or “so-called stalwarts” as he called them, after they had declined participation in a compromise two-day discussion on the state of the party, rather than the requested separate consultative conference.
How has Khoza become what could be described as the poster woman for a vote of conscience?
In Parliament since 2014 – she was placed seventh on the list from KwaZulu-Natal where she was an MPL – Khoza served in the finance committee, often making insightful interventions, but was largely unknown. Much changed with last year’s interviews for a new public protector to take over from Thuli Madonsela. The hearings of the ad hoc committee she chaired were broadcast live, and as part of canvassing as wide an input as possible, Khoza also interacted with civil society organisations and others.
Khoza now is the chairperson of the public service and administration committee. There, according to News24, she butted heads in May with Minister in the Presidency Jeff Radebe over the quality of the Performance Monitoring and Evaluation Department he heads.
With a Ph.D in administration, Khoza’s currently studying further, and writing a book. On Tuesday she gave just a hint of another level of dynamics in the Byzantine manoeuvrings within the governing ANC, describing it as a “very bad sentiment against clever blacks”.
When the motion of no confidence was first scheduled, former president Kgalema Motlanthe in April indicated that a vote of conscience was not misconduct. Both the ANC constitution and parliamentary rules are silent on this. “Those people are not hirelings of the ANC. They are public representatives. They take an oath as parliamentarians to be public representatives. They can’t be treated the same way as you treat an ANC branch,”.

This issue, like so many others in the ANC from monopoly capital to land reform, highlights the deep fissures in an organisation trying to straddle a rather schizophrenic view of itself – both as a modern political party and Africa’s oldest liberation movement.
Mbalula, in his capacity as the ANC’s head of organisation and speaking at the party’s national policy conference, could smoothly claim: “MPs are sworn in constitutionally. They owe their allegiance to the party.” After stating the ANC could not allow anyone from its ranks to support opposition parties, Mbalula added that if anyone defied the party line the ANC would “deal with it, rest assured, according to the constitution of the ANC”. That means disciplinary action.
For some in the ANC the nature of the vote would not matter: the party line rejecting the opposition no confidence vote in Zuma would hold whether the vote is in the open or secret. Or as last Friday’s ANC parliamentary caucus statement said on voting against the no confidence motion: “We have consistently been on record that we will not vote with the opposition to remove our ANC government from office immaterial whether such a motion is voted upon through an open or secret ballot.”
Whether a secret ballot will give succour to those in the ANC not wanting to toe the party line, or whether it opens the door to manipulation and further secret dealings that could undermine South Africa’s constitutional democracy, will no doubt be a subject of much discussion.
For Khoza it’s clear. “We are not defending ANC policies and noble mission, we are defending a leader who may arguably be described as someone with a chronically impaired moral reflective capacity,” she posted on Facebook on 7 July on the no confidence vote, also arguing: “To remain silent and unprincipled in times of crisis is tantamount to fuelling it. When this happens we subject ourselves to autopilot paralysis.”
And it was what she reiterated on Tuesday night. “I’m already out there,” And she’ll take the consequences from the ANC, which she calls her political home since the age of 12.

Press Release:


Dr Makhosi Khoza
Internal factions continue to divide some political parties, with members facing death threats and intimidation for speaking out. ANC MP Dr
Makhosi Khoza remains defiant however, as she continues to speak out on issues plaguing the ruling party. Carte Blanche asks: What is the
cost of courage in South Africa’s political arena?

Script:


MAKHOSI KHOZA FINAL SCRIPT TX SUNDAY 6TH AUGUST FOR VO

Commentary One
The announcement that set the tone for 2017 …

President Jacob Zuma
I have decided to make changes to the National Executive

Commentary Two
When the president fired Finance Minister Pravin Gordhan, and his deputy Mcebisi Jonas, his top officials like Gwede Mantashe, questioned the decision. But it was their dramatic about turn that shocked one of the party’s own, ANC MP Dr. Makhosi Khoza

Makhosi Khoza
There you had the leadership – the deputy president, Gwede Mantashe and the Treasurer general, they go out and say, hey! we don’t know where this decision was taken from, and before you know it they backtrack

Commentary Three
Angered, citizens took to the streets countrywide to protest that decision, one which later led to the downgrade of South Africa to junk status.

Up sound

From her hometown, in Pietermaritzburg, Khoza watched the countrywide marchers, and then read how the ANC had described the protest

Makhosi
It was more like the leadership was labelling people as racist and to me I didn’t see racism, I saw people united behind the South African flag with a common grievance: ‘ It’s no longer about us anymore’

Commentary Four
Two days later, Makhosi Khoza could no longer keep silent and posted her thoughts on Facebook

“Politics of patronage has finally claimed the sanity of my ANC leadership. A triumphant story has turned tragic in my life time. The ANC is defining itself out of power when the majority of its people remain trapped in poverty, joblessness, dependency on state social grants, poor quality education & health care…”

Makhosi Khoza
And an hour later my daughter comes into my room. Mom what have you done? You are trending on twitter. Did you write something?



Commentary Five
It was Khoza who was largely behind the transparent process of selecting the public protector, and Khoza who impressed at the parliamentary enquiry of the SABC. But since that Facebook post, she is almost a household name, because Khoza has repeatedly called for President Jacob Zuma to step down

Up sound KHOZA
Please Mr. President step down and respect those who elected you

Commentary six
Independent political analyst Professor Tinyiko Maluleke

Professor Maluleke
I think that speech may gain in importance as we look back at this moment when a bona fida, senior member of parliament made the call for the President to step down.

Makhosi Khoza
This is a president when black intellectuals express their views he does not agree with them he sarcastically labels them clever blacks. I am a black! I am clever! I am smart! I am educated, and therefore there is absolutely nothing wrong with that!

Applause

Professor Maluleke
This may be more important than what happens on Tuesday, the conversation we are having, is a lot more important, and Makhosi Khoza and several others like her will feature very highly in our memory of what has happened now

LINK
But her detractors have lashed out. The KZN women’s league have called her unscrupulous, the youth league, an un-rehabilitated delinquent. Clearly, she has touched a nerve.

Commentary Seven
But Khoza says the ANC has been her political home since she was 12

Bongani
Are you deliberately provoking the leadership?
Makhosi
If the leadership decides to feel provoked it’s their own business. What I am trying to say that there is a child you molded. If you are going to betray those value systems that you socialized me in, you must expect that I am going to revolt
Bongani
They say its ill-discipline?
Makhosi
Extreme ill –discipline! And guess what? That means if what I am doing is extreme ill discipline, that means corruption is now the moral signature of the ANC, which is really unfortunate





Commentary eight
Khoza is facing a disciplinary in September. Police minister Fikile Mbalula has equated resistance like hers to that of suicide bombers, but she says all she has done is chosen the interests of South Africans above their leader.

Makhosi Khoza
I am charged because I chose people, and not him!

LINK
There have been nearly 90 political assassinations in KZN since 2014, and it is her home province, so she was under no illusions that she is now under threat when she received a chilling WhatsApp message

Makhosi Khoza
I believe that is the lowest state you can get to in a democracy. In fact, that is the end of democracy.

Commentary nine
The WhatsApp gave her 21 days to live and Khoza no longer lives at home. Eventually the police ministry offered her protection but she politely declined

Makhosi
I think its disingenuous to say you can protect me as the minister when you have not provided me protection, and secondly when your own deputy minister is going around alleging I am DA, and I am the enemy of the people

Commentary Ten
She also believes the ANC tends to be tougher on women

Makhosi Khoza
I really really don’t think as women we should be intimidated. There is a tendency in the ANC to deal harshly with women and WHY HAVENT WE CHARGED PRESIDENT ZUMA IN THE ANC? WHY HAVENT WE?! THIS IS SOMEONE WHO HAS REPEATEDLY BROUGHT THE NAME OF THE ANC INTO DISREPUTE. THIS IS SOMEONE WHO HAS VIOLATED ALMOST EVERY SINGLE RULE IN THE CONSTITUTION OF THE ANC, LET ALONE THE CONSTITUTION OF THE COUNTRY, BUT THAT PERSON HAS NEVER BEEN BROUGHT BEFORE A DISCIPLINARY HEARING.

Commentary eleven
It’s all too familiar for Former public Protector Thuli Madonsela has been there. She too had death threats and was sent a dead cat

Thuli Madonsela
When you to speak truth to power, you may have to face headwinds. What we are seeing
in SA, happening with impunity is unacceptable and the level is shocking. We have seen what has happened to Makhosi Khoza. I would have expected some of the senior leaders to say No, not in my name

Prof Tinyiko Maluleke
One of the most shameful things of this moment is how easy it is to send SMS to say you have 20 days to live, how easy to walk into a press gathering and disrupt it and the silence from the powers that be- I haven’t heard the president saying anything about this

LINK
It’s not the first time Makhosi Khoza is rattling political cages. Having gone after corruption, she quit local government in 2012 after receiving threats. But this time they are not only going after her.

Bongani
WHAT has this done to your family?
Makhosi
To my kids …ya that part is the most difficult (she begins to cry)
Bongani
How is your daughter?
Well if they had threatened me alone, maybe I would cope. Not my children.
Bongani
Because we tried to get an interview before, and you cancelled because they threatened your daughter
Makhosi
I mean my daughter is being followed each day and Mbalula said there is no threats on my children. My children shouldn’t be punished because I as their mother have taken a particular position- at my level I will do it, but don’t touch my children!

Commentary twelve
At the time Thuli Madonsela’s children were also threatened

Bongani
What is it like to live in that cauldron?
Thuli
It was only now that I am at Harvard and at a distance and say Good Lord how did I get through that, how did my children get through that, how did my staff get through that

LINK
Tuesday’s motion of no confidence against the president is going to be the moment of truth. Will Makhosi Khoza stand alone, or will other ANC MPS join her in her quest to remove number one?



Makhosi
There are so, so, many comrades, I get e mails and calls, so many comrades are tired, but unfortunately, we don’t have the same level of courage
Bongani
All eyes will be on you on Tuesday, what are you going to do?
Makhosi
I have taken a stand. I am siding with the people and I am sorry Mr. President. I am not going to side with him

Commentary thirteen
Tuesday will be the eighth motion of no confidence against President Zuma. Political Analyst Stephen Grootes is unconvinced it will succeed.

Bongani
You say it’s not in the ANC interests of the ANC MPS- even those against him, to vote against him?
Stephen
Yes/ we mustn’t forget the real prize in the ANC at the moment is not the removal of JZ, it’s to win control of a fully functional non- split ANC in December. If there is a vote to remove JZ the ANC will split right down the middle. I don’t know if the December conference will even happen after that! Don’t forget the real prize for the opposition right now is an early election and the ANC knows it cannot fight an election now

Commentary fourteen
But even if the president remains in office, there is still the matter of the 783 charges

Bongani
Should he be charged?
Makhosi
Of course! He has to be charged. There is a tendency in the ANC to sub delegate its responsibility. Whenever there is a matter- ‘No push it to the commission!’ but we have our own constitution
Bongani
So, you continue to shake this tree?
Makhosi Khoza
I have no option, I love my country so much and I am tired of black South Africans being synonymous with corruption. I am tired because it vulgarizes all of us. I am tired of us as black Africans being portrayed as people who share collective stupidity. Most of the states that have failed in Africa – they failed not necessarily because the policies were wrong, it’s because the leaders became corrupt and they were standing on amoral ground. You cannot pursue a noble cause, if you are standing on an amoral platform.


THE END



PROMO One 10 seconds
Makhosi Khoza speaks out against President Zuma. But at what cost
Makhosi
At my level I will do it, but don’t touch my children


PROMO TWO 15 seconds
ANC MP Makhosi Khoza has been rattling political cages ahead of the no confidence motion against the president
Makhosi
AND WHY HAVENT WE CHARGED PRESIDENT ZUMA IN THE ANC? WHY HAVENT WE?!


PROMO THREE
Tension mounts ahead of this week’s no confidence vote against the president
Bongani
All eyes will be on you on Tuesday, what are you going to do?
Makhosi
I have taken a stand. I am siding with the people and I am sorry Mr. President. I am not going to side with him



TAKEN FROM MAKHOSI KHOZA ACTUAL PAGE

Politics of patronage has finally claimed the sanity of my ANC leadership. A triumphant story has turned tragic in my life time. The ANC is defining itself out of power when the majority of its people remain trapped in poverty, joblessness, dependency on state social grants, poor quality education & health care and when millions cross African colonial boarders in search for a better life in African soil as all boarders outside Africa offer no better prospects for them. As Africans we are a homogeneous lot. We are known as a "Shackled Continent" as defined by Guest a British journalist. Millions die of Malaria & malnutrition in the continent I call home.
The South African tragedy is an African continent catastrophe. I wish my ANC leaders could see what I see. I wish my ANC leadership could feel what I feel. I wish they can understand that indecision is tantamount to giving DA, EFF ... power on a silver platter.
Worse... it is continuous entrapment of the poor & marginalized in hopelessness. As a former student in Zimbabwe during the introduction of Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP) whatever conspiracy theories we may have, what I know for sure is that disinvestment in the South African economy is catastrophic in every imaginable manner.

.

Carte Blanche HD Nikola Vrahimis 30 August 2017 Press Release: Dr Makhosi Khoza Internal factions continue to divide some political parties, with members facing death threats and intimidation for speaking out. ANC MP Dr Makhosi Khoza remains defiant however, as she continues to speak out on issues plaguing the ruling party. Carte Blanche asks: What is the cost of courage in South Africa’s political arena? Script: MAKHOSI KHOZA FINAL SCRIPT TX SUNDAY 6TH AUGUST FOR VO Commentary One The announcement that set the tone for 2017 … President Jacob Zuma I have decided to make changes to the National Executive Commentary Two When the president fired Finance Minister Pravin Gordhan, and his deputy Mcebisi Jonas, his top officials like Gwede Mantashe, questioned the decision. But it was their dramatic about turn that shocked one of the party’s own, ANC MP Dr. Makhosi Khoza Makhosi Khoza There you had the leadership – the deputy president, Gwede Mantashe and the Treasurer general, they go out and say, hey! we don’t know where this decision was taken from, and before you know it they backtrack Commentary Three Angered, citizens took to the streets countrywide to protest that decision, one which later led to the downgrade of South Africa to junk status. Up sound From her hometown, in Pietermaritzburg, Khoza watched the countrywide marchers, and then read how the ANC had described the protest Makhosi It was more like the leadership was labelling people as racist and to me I didn’t see racism, I saw people united behind the South African flag with a common grievance: ‘ It’s no longer about us anymore’ Commentary Four Two days later, Makhosi Khoza could no longer keep silent and posted her thoughts on Facebook “Politics of patronage has finally claimed the sanity of my ANC leadership. A triumphant story has turned tragic in my life time. The ANC is defining itself out of power when the majority of its people remain trapped in poverty, joblessness, dependency on state social grants, poor quality education & health care…” Makhosi Khoza And an hour later my daughter comes into my room. Mom what have you done? You are trending on twitter. Did you write something? Commentary Five It was Khoza who was largely behind the transparent process of selecting the public protector, and Khoza who impressed at the parliamentary enquiry of the SABC. But since that Facebook post, she is almost a household name, because Khoza has repeatedly called for President Jacob Zuma to step down Up sound KHOZA Please Mr. President step down and respect those who elected you Commentary six Independent political analyst Professor Tinyiko Maluleke Professor Maluleke I think that speech may gain in importance as we look back at this moment when a bona fida, senior member of parliament made the call for the President to step down. Makhosi Khoza This is a president when black intellectuals express their views he does not agree with them he sarcastically labels them clever blacks. I am a black! I am clever! I am smart! I am educated, and therefore there is absolutely nothing wrong with that! Applause Professor Maluleke This may be more important than what happens on Tuesday, the conversation we are having, is a lot more important, and Makhosi Khoza and several others like her will feature very highly in our memory of what has happened now LINK But her detractors have lashed out. The KZN women’s league have called her unscrupulous, the youth league, an un-rehabilitated delinquent. Clearly, she has touched a nerve. Commentary Seven But Khoza says the ANC has been her political home since she was 12 Bongani Are you deliberately provoking the leadership? Makhosi If the leadership decides to feel provoked it’s their own business. What I am trying to say that there is a child you molded. If you are going to betray those value systems that you socialized me in, you must expect that I am going to revolt Bongani They say its ill-discipline? Makhosi Extreme ill –discipline! And guess what? That means if what I am doing is extreme ill discipline, that means corruption is now the moral signature of the ANC, which is really unfortunate Commentary eight Khoza is facing a disciplinary in September. Police minister Fikile Mbalula has equated resistance like hers to that of suicide bombers, but she says all she has done is chosen the interests of South Africans above their leader. Makhosi Khoza I am charged because I chose people, and not him! LINK There have been nearly 90 political assassinations in KZN since 2014, and it is her home province, so she was under no illusions that she is now under threat when she received a chilling WhatsApp message Makhosi Khoza I believe that is the lowest state you can get to in a democracy. In fact, that is the end of democracy. Commentary nine The WhatsApp gave her 21 days to live and Khoza no longer lives at home. Eventually the police ministry offered her protection but she politely declined Makhosi I think its disingenuous to say you can protect me as the minister when you have not provided me protection, and secondly when your own deputy minister is going around alleging I am DA, and I am the enemy of the people Commentary Ten She also believes the ANC tends to be tougher on women Makhosi Khoza I really really don’t think as women we should be intimidated. There is a tendency in the ANC to deal harshly with women and WHY HAVENT WE CHARGED PRESIDENT ZUMA IN THE ANC? WHY HAVENT WE?! THIS IS SOMEONE WHO HAS REPEATEDLY BROUGHT THE NAME OF THE ANC INTO DISREPUTE. THIS IS SOMEONE WHO HAS VIOLATED ALMOST EVERY SINGLE RULE IN THE CONSTITUTION OF THE ANC, LET ALONE THE CONSTITUTION OF THE COUNTRY, BUT THAT PERSON HAS NEVER BEEN BROUGHT BEFORE A DISCIPLINARY HEARING. Commentary eleven It’s all too familiar for Former public Protector Thuli Madonsela has been there. She too had death threats and was sent a dead cat Thuli Madonsela When you to speak truth to power, you may have to face headwinds. What we are seeing in SA, happening with impunity is unacceptable and the level is shocking. We have seen what has happened to Makhosi Khoza. I would have expected some of the senior leaders to say No, not in my name Prof Tinyiko Maluleke One of the most shameful things of this moment is how easy it is to send SMS to say you have 20 days to live, how easy to walk into a press gathering and disrupt it and the silence from the powers that be- I haven’t heard the president saying anything about this LINK It’s not the first time Makhosi Khoza is rattling political cages. Having gone after corruption, she quit local government in 2012 after receiving threats. But this time they are not only going after her. Bongani WHAT has this done to your family? Makhosi To my kids …ya that part is the most difficult (she begins to cry) Bongani How is your daughter? Well if they had threatened me alone, maybe I would cope. Not my children. Bongani Because we tried to get an interview before, and you cancelled because they threatened your daughter Makhosi I mean my daughter is being followed each day and Mbalula said there is no threats on my children. My children shouldn’t be punished because I as their mother have taken a particular position- at my level I will do it, but don’t touch my children! Commentary twelve At the time Thuli Madonsela’s children were also threatened Bongani What is it like to live in that cauldron? Thuli It was only now that I am at Harvard and at a distance and say Good Lord how did I get through that, how did my children get through that, how did my staff get through that LINK Tuesday’s motion of no confidence against the president is going to be the moment of truth. Will Makhosi Khoza stand alone, or will other ANC MPS join her in her quest to remove number one? Makhosi There are so, so, many comrades, I get e mails and calls, so many comrades are tired, but unfortunately, we don’t have the same level of courage Bongani All eyes will be on you on Tuesday, what are you going to do? Makhosi I have taken a stand. I am siding with the people and I am sorry Mr. President. I am not going to side with him Commentary thirteen Tuesday will be the eighth motion of no confidence against President Zuma. Political Analyst Stephen Grootes is unconvinced it will succeed. Bongani You say it’s not in the ANC interests of the ANC MPS- even those against him, to vote against him? Stephen Yes/ we mustn’t forget the real prize in the ANC at the moment is not the removal of JZ, it’s to win control of a fully functional non- split ANC in December. If there is a vote to remove JZ the ANC will split right down the middle. I don’t know if the December conference will even happen after that! Don’t forget the real prize for the opposition right now is an early election and the ANC knows it cannot fight an election now Commentary fourteen But even if the president remains in office, there is still the matter of the 783 charges Bongani Should he be charged? Makhosi Of course! He has to be charged. There is a tendency in the ANC to sub delegate its responsibility. Whenever there is a matter- ‘No push it to the commission!’ but we have our own constitution Bongani So, you continue to shake this tree? Makhosi Khoza I have no option, I love my country so much and I am tired of black South Africans being synonymous with corruption. I am tired because it vulgarizes all of us. I am tired of us as black Africans being portrayed as people who share collective stupidity. Most of the states that have failed in Africa – they failed not necessarily because the policies were wrong, it’s because the leaders became corrupt and they were standing on amoral ground. You cannot pursue a noble cause, if you are standing on an amoral platform. THE END PROMO One 10 seconds Makhosi Khoza speaks out against President Zuma. But at what cost Makhosi At my level I will do it, but don’t touch my children PROMO TWO 15 seconds ANC MP Makhosi Khoza has been rattling political cages ahead of the no confidence motion against the president Makhosi AND WHY HAVENT WE CHARGED PRESIDENT ZUMA IN THE ANC? WHY HAVENT WE?! PROMO THREE Tension mounts ahead of this week’s no confidence vote against the president Bongani All eyes will be on you on Tuesday, what are you going to do? Makhosi I have taken a stand. I am siding with the people and I am sorry Mr. President. I am not going to side with him TAKEN FROM MAKHOSI KHOZA ACTUAL PAGE Politics of patronage has finally claimed the sanity of my ANC leadership. A triumphant story has turned tragic in my life time. The ANC is defining itself out of power when the majority of its people remain trapped in poverty, joblessness, dependency on state social grants, poor quality education & health care and when millions cross African colonial boarders in search for a better life in African soil as all boarders outside Africa offer no better prospects for them. As Africans we are a homogeneous lot. We are known as a "Shackled Continent" as defined by Guest a British journalist. Millions die of Malaria & malnutrition in the continent I call home. The South African tragedy is an African continent catastrophe. I wish my ANC leaders could see what I see. I wish my ANC leadership could feel what I feel. I wish they can understand that indecision is tantamount to giving DA, EFF ... power on a silver platter. Worse... it is continuous entrapment of the poor & marginalized in hopelessness. As a former student in Zimbabwe during the introduction of Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP) whatever conspiracy theories we may have, what I know for sure is that disinvestment in the South African economy is catastrophic in every imaginable manner. . metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Dr Makhosi Khoza puts her life on the line to speak truth to power
metadata.Further information: The ANC powers that be have yet to make a decision on whether to discipline ANC MP Makhosi Khoza for her outspokenness outside official governing party structures – from calling for a secret ballot in the vote of no confidence in President Jacob Zuma on 8 August, to some sharply critical comments on the troubled state of the ANC and its MPs. Described by ANC Chief Whip Jackson Mthembu as “extremely ill-disciplined” for her public comments on the sidelines of last week’s ANC national policy conference, the ANC in Parliament on Tuesday confirmed the matter has been referred up to Luthuli House head office for a decision on what to do next. Not only has Mthembu taken exception, it is understood also that ANC Secretary-General Gwede Mantashe is annoyed. After Mthembu issued a scathing media statement, saying his MP was casting aspersions on the morality of party colleagues – “We have again spoken to comrade Khoza and raised our extreme discomfort with her utterances in relation to caucus and the leadership of the ANC at large” – Khoza took to Facebook, again: “Is it really ill-discipline or liberation struggle credentials’ fatigue that keeps us imagining unity when we are clearly no longer pursuing the same mission? Is it ill-discipline or daring to tackle the big elephant in the room… Is it extreme ill-discipline to be intolerant of bad leadership and to uphold the Constitution? Is it ill-discipline to elect principles and ditching destructive personalities?” It’s not necessarily a case of going rogue. For Khoza, speaking out is also a way to protect herself. She’s received death threats while on a parliamentary oversight trip to Limpopo, has threats directed at her daughter and has faced other bullying tactics, like the provincial ANC Youth League posting her home address on social media. “I remain vulnerable and living under constant attacks, life threats and insults. No protection has been provided to me by Parliament though the ANC knows the volatility of my province, KZN (KwaZulu-Natal). The only reason I’m probably still alive is the heightened alertness of the public on my safety. Let me thank you South Africans for your overwhelming support,” Khoza wrote on Facebook last week. “It should be recalled that I opened two criminal cases at the police stations in Hillcrest and Limpopho [sic] after receiving death threats which have not stopped. I’m continuously stalked and intimidated for voicing my views on the vote of no confidence matter on a daily basis.” On Tuesday she was accompanied by one of those, whom she described as “some volunteers” looking after her. One of the “volunteers” looked somewhat perturbed at Khoza being mobbed, including by a group of youngsters wanting a selfie, or two or three, and her handling of a tricky question. “Why should my parents vote?” Co-incidentally, her response was, of course they must vote. The conundrum on a vote of conscience or toeing the party line Khoza faces is not hers alone. Also in a tight spot are several other ANC MPs who have expressed their disquiet privately and publicly. Ditto members of the ANC alliance partners, the South African Communist Party (SACP) and trade union federation Cosatu, who have come to Parliament on an ANC ticket. Will the ANC line prevail, or will it be the resolutions of their organisations which both called for Zuma to step down that prevail? In the SACP at least there are ongoing discussions around this, according to at least one insider, although only Sunday’s closing of the SACP congress will show whether the self-proclaimed workers’ vanguard will take a firm resolution on how to cast the no-confidence ballot. Speaking out, like cleaning up the web of patronage-related tenders, can be a dangerous business in a party in which factionalism often goes hand in hand with violence. The SACP has objected to protests outside the house of its Second Deputy General-Secretary Solly Mapaila, the face of anti-state capture from within the alliance, but also violence against its members in Mpumalanga and last year’s killings in KwaZulu-Natal’s Inchanga. Police a year ago announced they were investigating 29 politically motivated killings and attempted murders, including of municipal managers and councillors. In late May this year, Police Minister Fikile Mbalula announced a task-team to look particularly at such killings in KwaZulu-Natal. Sometimes the response is more verbal as criticism itself becomes a tool in the current factional battles. Zuma delivered a snotklap to ANC veterans, or “so-called stalwarts” as he called them, after they had declined participation in a compromise two-day discussion on the state of the party, rather than the requested separate consultative conference. How has Khoza become what could be described as the poster woman for a vote of conscience? In Parliament since 2014 – she was placed seventh on the list from KwaZulu-Natal where she was an MPL – Khoza served in the finance committee, often making insightful interventions, but was largely unknown. Much changed with last year’s interviews for a new public protector to take over from Thuli Madonsela. The hearings of the ad hoc committee she chaired were broadcast live, and as part of canvassing as wide an input as possible, Khoza also interacted with civil society organisations and others. Khoza now is the chairperson of the public service and administration committee. There, according to News24, she butted heads in May with Minister in the Presidency Jeff Radebe over the quality of the Performance Monitoring and Evaluation Department he heads. With a Ph.D in administration, Khoza’s currently studying further, and writing a book. On Tuesday she gave just a hint of another level of dynamics in the Byzantine manoeuvrings within the governing ANC, describing it as a “very bad sentiment against clever blacks”. When the motion of no confidence was first scheduled, former president Kgalema Motlanthe in April indicated that a vote of conscience was not misconduct. Both the ANC constitution and parliamentary rules are silent on this. “Those people are not hirelings of the ANC. They are public representatives. They take an oath as parliamentarians to be public representatives. They can’t be treated the same way as you treat an ANC branch,”. This issue, like so many others in the ANC from monopoly capital to land reform, highlights the deep fissures in an organisation trying to straddle a rather schizophrenic view of itself – both as a modern political party and Africa’s oldest liberation movement. Mbalula, in his capacity as the ANC’s head of organisation and speaking at the party’s national policy conference, could smoothly claim: “MPs are sworn in constitutionally. They owe their allegiance to the party.” After stating the ANC could not allow anyone from its ranks to support opposition parties, Mbalula added that if anyone defied the party line the ANC would “deal with it, rest assured, according to the constitution of the ANC”. That means disciplinary action. For some in the ANC the nature of the vote would not matter: the party line rejecting the opposition no confidence vote in Zuma would hold whether the vote is in the open or secret. Or as last Friday’s ANC parliamentary caucus statement said on voting against the no confidence motion: “We have consistently been on record that we will not vote with the opposition to remove our ANC government from office immaterial whether such a motion is voted upon through an open or secret ballot.” Whether a secret ballot will give succour to those in the ANC not wanting to toe the party line, or whether it opens the door to manipulation and further secret dealings that could undermine South Africa’s constitutional democracy, will no doubt be a subject of much discussion. For Khoza it’s clear. “We are not defending ANC policies and noble mission, we are defending a leader who may arguably be described as someone with a chronically impaired moral reflective capacity,” she posted on Facebook on 7 July on the no confidence vote, also arguing: “To remain silent and unprincipled in times of crisis is tantamount to fuelling it. When this happens we subject ourselves to autopilot paralysis.” And it was what she reiterated on Tuesday night. “I’m already out there,” And she’ll take the consequences from the ANC, which she calls her political home since the age of 12.
